task_definition.task_name: Back Azimuth Estimation Using BazNet on Continuous Waveform

task_description.overview: Estimate seismic backazimuth from three‐component continuous waveform data using a pretrained deep neural network (BazNet).
steps: Load the pretrained BazNet model and weights, move it to the appropriate device (CPU or GPU), and set it to evaluation mode.
Read continuous three‐component seismic waveform data in MiniSEED or similar format using ObsPy.

Convert the waveform traces into a NumPy array of shape [3, N], where N ≥ 6000 samples, and normalize each channel by subtracting its mean and dividing by its standard deviation or maximum absolute value.
Trim or pad the normalized data to exactly 6000 samples per channel.
Convert the NumPy array to a PyTorch tensor, add a batch dimension, and transfer it to the same device as the model.
Run the forward pass through the BazNet model to get sine and cosine components of the backazimuth prediction.
Compute the backazimuth angle in degrees via arctangent of the predicted sine and cosine outputs.

task_definition.agent_prompt: Back azimuth estimation using `baz_network` deep learning model on the continuous three-component waveform data. Load and normalize the continuous three-component waveform file at {waveform_path} with the specific {normalize_mode} mode. The pretrained baz_network model is located at {checkpoint_path} and its related parameters are {model_params}. Run inference by feeding the specific waveform segment from {start_point} to {end_point} into the model to obtain a single back azimuth estimate, and save the estimated value into a json file {result_data.file_name} with content {result_data.file_content}. Finally, plot a figure to show the waveform with the predicted back azimuth estimation results and save it to {waveform_with_baz}.
